# The Arcade > 18 self-contained pages that teach eleven subjects to a child: a hub, 16 games, and a daily-session page. No build step, no accounts, no network — everything inline or beside the page, progress in localStorage. No third-party library is loaded or vendored: the entire runtime is the 18 pages plus their sibling `.js` files. The one imported code is 26 MIT-licensed Colorfigures demo figures in `figures/`, copied whole and unmodified, each already a single self-contained file. This folder has its own git repository (branch `main`, no remote), but the parent `games` repo still tracks these files too — see README "This repository" before committing arcade work from the parent.

## Where to start

- **New to the folder**: this file, then README (what everything is and how a game is built), then `docs/design.md` (why each interaction is shaped the way it is).
- **About to change code**: `dev-llms.txt` — state shapes, function index with line numbers, the shared deck mechanism, and the list of known defects.
- **About to restyle anything**: `docs/design.md` first. Every token has a reason and several were removed on purpose.

## The hard invariants (break these and the product changes, not the code)

- [Offline-only](index.html): zero `fetch`, zero `XMLHttpRequest`, zero external fonts or icon
  fonts across all 18 pages, and no third-party library at all. Any new asset must be inline SVG
  or a sibling `.js`/`.png` file. A page that pulls from a CDN is a broken guarantee, not a slow
  page. Probe: wire a `request` listener in Playwright and assert every URL starts with the served
  base; then load the page from `file://` with `context.set_offline(True)` and assert it still
  initialises. Canary the probe with a planted CDN `<link>` — a network check that has never
  failed is not a network check. The framed figures count: navigate the top page and assert
  `page.frames[-1]` has its `<svg>` and its buttons, because a blank frame throws nothing in its
  parent.
- [Paper design system](docs/design.md): `--paper:#fdf7ea`, `--ink:#191c3a`, 2.5px borders, hard
  offset shadows (`6px 6px 0 var(--ink)`), `ui-rounded` first font, `html{font-size:17px}`,
  `1.05rem`/`1.5` body. Nothing glows, blurs, or floats. The one spectacle is the confetti burst,
  bounded by `prefers-reduced-motion`. The figures in `figures/` are the sanctioned exception:
  third-party pages with their own palette, framed rather than restyled. Full rationale with the
  reason for every token in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md) — read it before restyling anything.
- [Session alternation](session.js): the 11 subjects are 5 languages (`kind:'lang'`: spelling,
  french, chinese, swahili, calligraphy) + 6 others (`kind:'other'`: maths, physics, chemistry,
  typing, piano, howthingswork). The order alternates for as long as the counts allow, and there
  is a load-time `checkOrder()` that throws if two `lang` subjects end up adjacent or if the plan
  does not open on a language. Six others against five languages makes strict alternation
  impossible while spelling stays first, so exactly one `other`-`other` pair is expected, at the
  end (piano, howthingswork). Adding a subject means adding a `kind` and re-slotting; the guard
  will catch a wrong slot but not a missing one.
- [Decks are 50, and the size is per family](number-bonds.html): maths drills and the spelling bee
  declare `const TOTAL = 50`; languages (`lang-engine.js`, `cfg.total`) are 30; sciences
  (`science-engine.js`, `cfg.total`) are 20; calligraphy 20. The deck is the unit of completion.
  Pools are *generated* (`poolFor(level)`, `factsFor(mode,table)`), never stored — no
  question exists to delete. Freshness maps (`seen: {bucket:{key:ts}}`), stamped on *served* not
  *built*, capped (SEEN_CAP 900 in the five drills, 1400 in the spelling bee, 1200 in the
  language, science and piano engines, 600 in the arena), oldest-dropped. A deck smaller than its
  pool cycles with a pass counter so the fill loop cannot spin.
- [Three completion markers](session.js): stage games toggle `#done` class `on` (`class="stage"`:
  languages, calligraphy, spelling bee, physics, chemistry, how things work); maths/typing toggle
  `#done` class `show` (`class="done"`); `infinite-arena.html` alone shows `#summaryPanel` class
  `show`.
  `session.js` reads the marker the page *declares* via the element's own class — accepting
  either marker on any page lets a class a game never uses count as finished
  (`.stage.on` is true on a stage game's home screen). A new game must declare one of these shapes.
- [localStorage versioning](index.html): every key is `arcade.<game>.v<N>`; bump the version when
  the shape changes, never reuse a key with a new shape. `arcade.session.v1` is trimmed to
  `KEEP_DAYS = 120` on write.

## The engines

- [lang-engine.js](lang-engine.js): one quiz engine for French, Kiswahili and Mandarin (spelling
  bee carries its own engine in `spelling-bee.html`). Mode
  buttons, deck queue, answering, scoring, the tick that flips `#done`. Page supplies a bank and
  target. Does not know about lessons.
- [piano-engine.js](piano-engine.js): the piano course. Draws the staff from each note's diatonic
  index (`staffSvg`), lays out a two-octave keyboard (`keyboardHtml`), synthesises pitch with
  oscillators (`playNote`/`playChord`/`playSeq` — no audio assets, so the offline guarantee holds),
  and runs a play stage that waits for the learner rather than the clock. One bank, three answer
  channels: `read` (staff shown), `hear` (staff hidden, played), `find` (press the key; judged on
  pitch class, not MIDI).
- [science-engine.js](science-engine.js): quiz engine for physics and chemistry **plus the lesson
  system**. `render()` checks each question's topic against `state.taught` (persisted alongside the
  freshness map) and, on a topic's first encounter, shows the lesson before the question. Resume
  modes: `'keep'` returns to the same question, `'render'` re-renders, otherwise home. Topic chips
  carry a `.tick` (taught) or `.new` badge. `esc()` everything that passes `innerHTML`; SVG figure
  markup is the one sanctioned exception (caption still escaped).
- [maths-engine.js](maths-engine.js): shared by the five maths drills. Owns the freshness deck
  (`freshFirst`/`markSeen`/`newCycle`, each taking the drill's own `keyOf`), the oscillators
  (`tone`/`goodSound`/`badSound`), the confetti canvas (mounted lazily, reusing a page's existing
  `#confetti` rather than adding a second one) and the lesson overlay. Does **not** own the
  interaction — bonds drag a divider, the column drills animate base-ten blocks, times tables step
  an array, division deals cookies. `init({topics, lessons})` mounts a fixed-position **Learn**
  button; the dialog injects its own CSS so it takes the palette of whichever page it is on.

## Content banks (data beside the page, never inline)

- [spelling-bank.js](spelling-bank.js) 1,239 graded words (315 / 379 / 545 across three tiers) · [french-bank.js](french-bank.js)
  words+sentences · [swahili-bank.js](swahili-bank.js) noun classes ·
  [chinese-bank.js](chinese-bank.js) characters+pinyin+gloss ·
  [calligraphy-bank.js](calligraphy-bank.js) 440 characters with stroke order ·
  [calligraphy-sketch.js](calligraphy-sketch.js) hand-drawn pictograms + composition sketches ·
- [piano-bank.js](piano-bank.js): 181 questions across ten topics, generated where the content is
  systematic (every staff position, every interval, every key signature) and authored where it is
  not; plus 8 public-domain pieces as `{id, title, note, notes:[{m,b}]}`. [piano-lessons.js](piano-lessons.js):
  10 lessons keyed by topic id, same shape as the science lessons, two inline SVG figures each.
- [physics-bank.js](physics-bank.js) · [chemistry-bank.js](chemistry-bank.js): questions by topic,
  each with an explanation written for the *explanation screen*, not the lesson. Lesson text is
  never derived from the bank (spoiler) or from explanations (answers with questions stripped).

## Lessons + figures

- [physics-lessons.js](physics-lessons.js) · [chemistry-lessons.js](chemistry-lessons.js): 10 each,
  key = bank topic id. Shape:
  `{ title, why, rule, beats[2-3], example{q,steps[2+],a}, remember, trap, figs[2]{cap,svg} }`.
  `example` uses numbers the bank never asks — the lesson must not hand over a bank answer. Every
  lesson carries ≥2 inline SVG figures; the probe checks overflow and zero-height at 390px.
- [maths-lessons.js](maths-lessons.js): 20 lessons, 4 per drill, keyed
  `MATHS_LESSONS['<drill-id>'] → {topics:[{id,name}], lessons:{<topic-id>: lesson}}`. Same shape as
  the science lessons. They are **opened, not scheduled** — a maths drill has modes and a generated
  pool, so there is no "first question on this topic" to hang an automatic lesson on. The overlay
  is a dialog, not a stage, because the five drills have five different stage machines.

## The machine shelf

- [how-things-work.html](how-things-work.html) · [figures/](figures/): 26 MIT-licensed Colorfigures
  demo figures by April Zhu, copied whole and unmodified, licence in
  [figures/LICENSE-colorfigures.txt](figures/LICENSE-colorfigures.txt). Each figure is a complete
  page — isometric model, drag-to-turn camera, working buttons, a See-through mode that ghosts the
  case and draws the real parts, and Labels that light the moving one.
- The wrapper is deliberately thin: it shows one figure in an `<iframe>`, prints the author's own
  title, hint and (where one exists) "big idea" line, and lists the other 25 in six groups. Do not
  re-describe the machines there — a second source of truth the figures cannot correct.
- **Frame, don't inline.** Each figure sets `document.body.innerHTML` at mount and ships its own
  `:root`, so inlining it would overwrite the page. `file://` lets the frame render in Chromium,
  WebKit and Firefox but **not** read across it in Chromium or WebKit, so the frame height is fixed
  (820 px, 740 px on a phone), measured against the tallest of the 26 rather than fitted at runtime.
- 7 of the 26 ship without an `idea` line; the page shows none for those. Do not invent one.
- Record: `arcade.howthingswork.v1` = `{ v, explored:{slug:ts}, perGroup:{group:pct}, day }`.
  One machine met is the day's sitting. `perGroup` exists only so the hub's star rating can read
  this record like any other game's bucket.

## Session state shape

- [session.js](session.js) reads/writes `arcade.session.v1` =
  `{ v:1, days:{ 'YYYY-MM-DD': { done:{ subjectId: timestamp } } } }`, local date (not UTC), trimmed
  to 120 days. Exposes `window.ArcadeSession` → `{ plan(), progress(), mark(), streak(), history(n),
  dayKey, isFinished }`. Any game page loads it so finishing a deck can toast the next subject.

## How to verify a change

- Serve on a private port, drive with Playwright, assert on the DOM:
  `http.server` + `socketserver` with `allow_reuse_address`, `functools.partial(SimpleHTTPRequestHandler,
  directory=<this folder>)`, thread the serve loop, then `p.chromium.launch()` and navigate.
- Assertions that matter, in order: **no `pageerror`**, **no request outside the served base**,
  every new feature's promised count (`>= 2` figures per lesson), **no overflow at 390px viewport**
  (the design's first width), figure `getBoundingClientRect().height > 40` (no collapsed SVG).
- Probes are throwaway scripts in `/tmp` — recreate from this recipe, do not hunt for them.
- Canary each probe: plant the defect, watch the probe fail, restore from a backup, confirm
  byte-identical. A probe that has never failed has tested nothing.

## The three failure modes this codebase has actually produced (hunt for these by name)

1. **A predicate that is a strict subset of what it tests** — accepting either completion marker
   is the canonical instance. Ask "what does this NOT check?"
2. **A gate that passes on a construction error** — a probe whose fixture broke reads as a suite
   failing wholesale; read the failure *reason*, not the count.
3. **Colliding names** — `.note` meaning one thing in a step row and another on the page; an id
   the engine and the tracker both use. Check for id/class collision when adding any element.

## Optional

- [docs/design.md](docs/design.md): the design narrative — every game's pedagogy, why
  deck = 50, why `ui-rounded`, why cream over white, why the confetti is the only spectacle, why
  the uppercase micro-type was removed. Read before substantive UI work here.
- [dev-llms.txt](dev-llms.txt): the implementation reference — exact state shapes, the function
  index per file, the shared deck mechanism, and the known defects.
- `docs/design.md` lives inside this repository; the frontend app that served it before reads the
  same path, so both checkouts see the same file.
